body:
## 背景

API Schema Plannerにより、GitHub IssueからOpenAPI 3.1ベースのAPI Schema Proposalを生成し、人間がレビュー・承認できるようになった。

一方で、現状はAPI Schemaを承認した後に、その契約を使ってFrontendがRails APIの完成を待たずに開発できるMock Serverがない。

このままだとContract-FirstでAPI仕様を先に確定しても、Frontend / Backendの並行開発に十分つながらない。

そのため、**承認済みOpenAPIからローカルMock Serverを起動できる仕組み**を追加する。

---

## 目的

API Schema Plannerで承認されたOpenAPIをそのままMock APIとして利用できるようにし、Expo / React AdminがRails API完成前からAPI接続・画面実装を開始できるようにする。

```text
GitHub Issue
  ↓
API Schema Planner
  ↓
OpenAPI Proposal
  ↓
Human Review / Approval
  ↓
Mock Server
  ├─ Expo
  └─ React Admin

同時並行
  ↓
Rails API実装
```

---

## 基本方針

初期実装ではOpenAPI 3.1からMock Serverを起動できる既存ツールを利用する。

第一候補は **Prism** とする。

理由:

- OpenAPIからそのままMock Serverを起動できる
- 独自Mock APIを実装しなくてよい
- Contract-Firstの流れと相性がよい
- Frontend / Backendが同じOpenAPIを参照できる

ただし、実装時にPrismより適切な選択肢がある場合は比較のうえ変更してよい。

---

## 想定コマンド

例:

```bash
pnpm api:mock https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number>
```

または責務上より自然であれば、以下のような形式でもよい。

```bash
pnpm api:mock --schema .harness/api-schema/<issue-number>/openapi.yaml
```

CLIインターフェースは実装時に確定する。

---

## Mock Server起動条件

未承認のAPI SchemaをFrontendが契約として利用しないようにする。

Issue URLを入力とする場合は、以下を確認する。

```text
planner:api-schema-status
        ↓
APPROVED ?
  ├─ No  → 起動しない
  └─ Yes → Mock Server起動
```

承認判定のSource of Truthは既存のAPI Schema Approvalとし、`api-schema-approved`ラベルだけを信用しない。

Mock Serverが使用するOpenAPIは、承認対象と同一digestのProposalであることを保証する。

---

## Mock APIの振る舞い

最低限以下を満たす。

- OpenAPIに定義されたpath / methodで応答できる
- response statusをOpenAPIから解釈できる
- response schemaに沿ったJSONを返せる
- array / object / enum / nullable等の基本schemaを扱える
- Cognito JWT必須endpointでも、ローカルMock用途として起動できる
- 実際のCognitoやRails APIへ接続しない
- Secret / Credentialの実値を要求・保存しない

認証必須endpointについては、初期段階では本物のJWT検証を行わず、Mock ServerとしてFrontend開発を妨げない方式とする。

必要であれば固定Bearer tokenや認証スキップ等を採用するが、**実Credentialは利用しない**。

---

## Frontendからの利用

Frontend側は環境変数等でAPI Base URLを切り替えられる前提とする。

例:

```text
Local Mock
http://localhost:4010

Development API
https://dev-api.example.com
```

Mock Server自身にExpo / React Admin固有のロジックは持たせない。

---

## OpenAPIとの関係

Mock Server用に別API仕様を持たない。

```text
Approved OpenAPI
      ↓
Mock Server
      ↓
Frontend

Approved OpenAPI
      ↓
Rails implementation
```

Frontend MockとRails APIが別々の契約を持つことを避け、**OpenAPIを共通Contractとして利用する**。

---

## 受け入れ要件

- [ ] 承認済みOpenAPIからローカルMock Serverを起動できる
- [ ] 未承認のAPI SchemaではMock Serverを起動しない
- [ ] `api-schema-approved`ラベルだけでは承認済みと判定しない
- [ ] 承認対象と同一digestのOpenAPIを利用する
- [ ] OpenAPI 3.1のpath / methodをMock APIとして提供できる
- [ ] OpenAPIのresponse schemaに沿ったJSONを返せる
- [ ] object / array / enum / nullableを最低限扱える
- [ ] Cognito JWT必須endpointをFrontend開発用にMockできる
- [ ] 本物のCognito / Rails API / Production APIへ接続しない
- [ ] Secret / Credential実値を必要としない
- [ ] FrontendからAPI Base URLを切り替えて利用できる設計にする
- [ ] Mock用の独自API仕様を持たずOpenAPIをSource of Truthにする
- [ ] 起動方法・利用方法をREADMEまたはdocsに記載する
- [ ] CI / Harnessの既存品質ゲートを壊さない

---

## 検証例

```text
Given API Schema ProposalがAPPROVEDである
When Mock Serverを起動する
Then OpenAPIに定義されたendpointへHTTPリクエストできる
And response schemaに沿ったJSONが返る
```

```text
Given API Schema Proposalが未承認である
When Mock Serverを起動しようとする
Then 起動を拒否する
And 未承認である理由を表示する
```

---

## 今回やらないこと

- Rails APIの自動実装
- Frontend API clientの自動生成
- OpenAPI code generation
- Production APIへの接続
- Cognitoの実JWT検証
- 本番相当の認証・認可Mock
- Statefulな業務ロジックの完全再現
- DBを持つ高機能Mock Backend
- 自動merge

---

## 完了後の位置づけ

```text
PBI
 ↓
SBI Planner
 ↓
API Schema Planner
 ↓
Human API Review / Approval
 ↓
Approved OpenAPI
 ├─ Mock Server → Expo / React Admin
 └─ Rails API implementation
 ↓
Contract / Acceptance Verification
```

API Schema Plannerで作った契約を実際の並行開発に使える状態までつなげることを目的とする。
title: 承認済みOpenAPIからローカルMock Serverを起動できるようにする

body:
## Summary

Requested on 2026-10-13, as three goals:

1. **Mock data ships with every integration** (in Tale's words, every _connector_) in a way that lets a workflow (an automation) be tested end to end before it goes into production, and that covers all cases.
2. **A test run changes nothing outside Tale, and still earns trust.** The mocks the integrations ship are what make it "bullet proof".
3. **Improve more generally how integrations work in Tale.** This part is deliberately open. Whoever takes this ticket, a person or an agent, may propose and make changes beyond the mocks. The evidence below shows where to look. It is not a scope.

This issue records what exists today, how a test run uses it, what a faithful mock would have to cover, and the design space, with no preferred answer. A follow-up, #4944, ranks the 1,000 integrations that matter most to businesses and opens one issue for each. It builds on whatever standard this ticket settles for shipped mocks.

Snapshot: `main` `0cf2c45fda` (2026-10-13).

## What exists today

### The catalog

- 22 connectors under `configs/platform/system/connectors/`, with 127 actions: 89 reads and 38 writes. 87 actions run a JavaScript body and 40 a native platform module.
- A connector is one `connector.yml` (plus an icon for 16 of them). No mock or fixture file lives beside any of them.
- Two actions are declared `idempotent`: `notify.member` and `task.create`, both the platform's own. No vendor write is. (`.agents/repo.md:800` still says no shipped action is.)
- Adding a connector is a source contribution. The runtime reads the platform catalog and has no organization-level upload (`docs/en/develop/connectors.md:43`).

### The mock an integration ships

- Every action must carry a `mock`: "Deterministic mock body (JS): `input` in scope, returns the mock output. Required — the authoring/test loop runs on it." (`packages/shared/src/schemas/connectors.ts:239-241`). The docs say the same: "Required deterministic JavaScript implementation; same input, same output, no network I/O" (`docs/en/develop/connectors.md:56`).
- Measured over all 127 mocks with a script over the `connector.yml` files (the patterns are heuristic): the median mock is 2 lines long; 26 (about a fifth) branch on their input at all; 2 can raise an error (both in `task`); none reads `ctx`, so none can remember anything between two calls; 17 mention paging fields. For example, `slack.list_channels` returns one fixed public channel and `next_cursor: null`, whatever it is asked.
- `output` is "documentation, not a runtime output validator" (`docs/en/develop/connectors.md:54`). The one catalog-wide check of the mocks runs each of them with its `exampleInput`, twice, and compares the two answers (`services/platform/lib/shared/schemas/shipped-connectors.test.ts:122-134`). Nothing compares a mock's answer with its action's declared output, or with what the vendor returns. 124 of the 127 actions have an `exampleInput`.

### What a test run does with it

- A run is `mock` or `live` (`services/platform/backend/core/automations/stepper.ts:432`). In mock mode a connector node resolves its input and checks it against the action's input schema. It then takes a stand-in output if the test gave one, and otherwise runs the action's `mock`; it records a write as an effect without performing it. In live mode it calls the action's live body (`services/platform/lib/engine/core/execute/index.ts:849-897`).
- The promise to the user: "Test run uses the selected saved version with deterministic mocks. It does not send mail or change external records." (`docs/en/platform/automations/editor.md:207`). Over MCP, `run_automation` runs a draft "on the deterministic mocks: nothing leaves Tale and nothing is stored" (`docs/en/develop/mcp-endpoint.md:136`).
- A workflow's acceptance tests can replace any node's call with a **stand-in output** (`mocks: node id → output`) or a **simulated failure** (`failures: node id → message`, worded "(simulated by the test)"), and then assert on the output, the effects and the node states (`services/platform/lib/engine/api/docs.ts:300-345`, `lib/engine/api/tests.ts`). So every case beyond the one canned answer is invented by the workflow's author, test by test, and nothing says it resembles what the vendor does.
- In mock mode a model node returns a deterministic default text and an agent node a deterministic default reply (`lib/engine/core/execute/scope.ts:77-85`). A mock run's results "were made up", so they cannot seed a live replay (`lib/engine/core/record/replay.ts:305`).
- Approvals are out of the picture: "A mock test does not prove that a live approval will appear" (`docs/en/platform/approvals/configure.md:29`).

### A second mock mechanism, outside the connectors

- `services/platform/lib/mocks/` is a Prism-based local gateway. It serves OpenAPI examples at `/mock/<connector>/*` for 10 vendor specs (Confluence, Discord, GitHub, Gmail, Google Drive, Microsoft Graph, Shopify, Slack, Tavily and Twilio, from a handful to a few dozen operations each) and for AI providers.
- Its README says: "The specs cover the operations they list, not every operation an upstream service offers", and "There is no blanket connector redirect wired into the current backend by setting `TALE_MOCK_CONNECTORS_BASE` alone." Its registry still names the retired Convex sandbox (`lib/mocks/registry.ts`).
- It is test infrastructure of the repository. It is not shipped with a connector, and a test run in the app cannot reach it.

### What the docs ask of a contributor

"Test three things separately when contributing: schema validation, deterministic mock behavior, and the live vendor path. Check failure handling as well as success: missing credential, wrong scope, denied destination, invalid input, vendor refusal, and an approval wait for writes." (`docs/en/develop/connectors.md:130`). Of the mocks, the shipped-catalog test checks only that each one runs and is deterministic (above); no catalog-wide test of the failure cases on that list was found.

## Neighbouring work

- **#4929** (open, `needs discussion`): stand-ins in durable runs, and a **preview mode**, "real connector reads and real model calls (billed, budgets apply), holds writes back as 'would have sent'". It records that "the owner said yes on 2026-10-08". A preview and a mock-only test run are two answers to "change nothing"; whatever this ticket settles has to fit the modes #4929 settles.
- **#4936** (epic), **#4927**, **#4928**: the engine's walkers. #4936 lists "a simulated 'fail once, then succeed' stand-in for tests" among the things it leaves out on purpose. A faithful mock set for retries and for an in-doubt write needs a case like it.
- **Known gaps in the contract ledger** (`.agents/repo.md`): an in-doubt step is decided in the app only (`:784`); the session-bound connector runner has no caller (`:474`).

## What "faithful" has to mean (considerations, not decisions)

1. **Cases per action.** Success; an empty result; not found; the first, a middle and the last page; a refusal of invalid input; credentials missing, expired or short of a scope; a rate limit with a wait; a timeout or outage; a partial failure inside a batch; a repeated request with the same idempotency key; a large payload; text in other encodings and languages.
2. **State.** Create then read, update then read, delete then read within one run. Per run, isolated, and discarded with the run.
3. **Shape fidelity.** The mock's answer matches the action's declared output and what the vendor really returns. How drift is found (against recorded real responses, against the vendor's own OpenAPI document, or against a vendor sandbox) and who is told.
4. **Writes.** A test run shows the write that would have happened (today an effect record) and the answer the vendor would give to it.
5. **Failure classes.** A live failure is classified, and the class decides whether a step is retried or parked in doubt. A simulated failure has to pass through the same classification, or a test cannot prove either behaviour.
6. **Data.** Synthetic only. `.agents/repo.md` keeps client names, fixtures and business rules out of the shared implementation, and this repository is public.
7. **Cost.** Mocks multiply by integrations: 22 today, and #4944 plans many more. What it costs to write and to review a mock per integration is the real constraint.

## Open design space (no preference stated; the assignee decides)

- **Where a mock lives.** In the connector's file (today), as files beside it, as a pack, generated from the vendor's OpenAPI document, or recorded from real traffic and scrubbed.
- **Where a test run swaps it in.** At the action (today); at the HTTP layer, so the real live body runs against a vendor-shaped mock (what `lib/mocks` does for tests); or both.
- **What a mock is.** A function (today); a table of scenarios (input matcher to response, errors included); a small stateful simulator; or an OpenAPI mock server (Prism is already in the repository).
- **How a test picks a case.** By input, by a scenario name per node, or from a library of named scenarios per integration; and how a failing scenario is written in a test.
- **How completeness is held.** A catalog gate in CI: each action ships a minimum set of scenario kinds (a read: success, empty, error; a write: success, refusal, duplicate).
- **Who writes them.** How a person, or an agent (the product's own over MCP, or a coding agent), writes and checks the mocks of a new integration.
- **Beyond mocks, "how integrations work".** Open. The evidence above points at: how credentials, consent and per-credential endpoints are declared; idempotency (2 of 38 writes are declared); the two failure and retry classes; the second mock mechanism; the lack of an organization-level connector upload (a source contribution or the generic `http` connector); the contributor flow and its docs; and how a call is observed. These are pointers, not a scope.

Maintained tools that already exist (each read on 2026-10-13): `stripe/stripe-mock` (MIT; "a mock HTTP server that responds like the real Stripe API", usable "instead of Stripe's testmode"), `stoplightio/prism` (Apache-2.0; already used in `lib/mocks`), `wiremock/wiremock` (Apache-2.0), `mockoon/mockoon` (MIT), `mswjs/msw` (MIT), `nock/nock` (MIT), and the Pact contract-testing framework.

## Constraints

- **Org configuration is files, not tables** (`.agents/repo.md`). If scenarios or mocks become organization-visible configuration, they follow that rule.
- **Tenant isolation.** Any mock state is per run and per organization, and never shared across organizations.
- **Isolation of code.** Mock bodies run in the code runner's sandbox today; a new form of mock keeps that boundary.
- **A domain's rules are a checked spec.** The automations and connectors specs, the manual boxes and the docs move with the change, in English, German and French, with accessibility held.
- **"Reach for a well-known, maintained library before hand-rolling"** (`AGENTS.md:137`).

## Questions

- Is the aim "no real change, ever" (a mock-only test run), or also "real reads, held writes" (the preview of #4929), as separate modes?
- Which cases count as "all cases", and who decides the list for each integration?
- Must a mock be checked against the real service on a schedule? That needs test accounts per vendor.
- Are the 22 shipped connectors the reference and upgraded first?
- Is a mock, with a minimum coverage, a required part of every connector, or optional per integration?

## Not examined

- The code of each vendor's live body, and how closely any mock matches its vendor today.
- Whether a vendor offers a sandbox or test accounts, per integration. Nothing was run against a real vendor.
- The org-level custom connector gap beyond what the docs say, and the MCP and REST surfaces for connectors.
- The patterns used for the measurements above are heuristic. The counts describe the mock bodies as text.

## Related

#4944 (the follow-up that ranks the integrations and opens one issue each), #4929, #4936, #4927, #4928.

Observed at `main` `0cf2c45fda` (2026-10-13).
title: Improvement: ship faithful mocks with every integration (connector), so a test run proves a workflow end to end and changes nothing outside Tale
